how_read: Pages read with scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py's own code through a small wrapper (.scratch/fetch_by_page.py, not committed). On 2026-11-09 mariowiki.com answered the reader's request by revision id (action=parse&oldid=...) and its plain-page fallback with HTTP 403, but answered the same render call asked by page name (action=parse&page=...). The wrapper changes only that one call: the licence line, the revision lookup and the text extraction are the reader's own, and the wrapper checks the revision the wiki rendered is the revision the reader looked up (no mismatch warning appeared). The revision below is the one the reader printed. Every quoted fragment was checked, by script, to occur word for word in the fetched page text (whitespace collapsed). The pages are kept in build/wiki-live/mariowiki/ in the helper's copy. Several pages describe the whole series; a line states a first-game fact only where the page says so for Mario Party (a page section for the first game, or a board or shop table of the first game).

lines.line: Summary: A board space that calls up Bowser to take your coins. Mario Party's first game has you spin a roulette that picks one event, from a plain coin fine to a minigame where the losers pay him.

quoted: Any player who lands on this space will meet Bowser, who triggers a roulette.

In the first Mario Party, Bowser appears to the player who lands on the Bowser Space in the usual background used for meeting characters on the board and forces them to spin a roulette wheel to decide the event.
Coins for Bowser: Bowser takes 10–50 Coins from that player.
Afterward, everyone aside from the winner of the minigame loses Coins to Bowser.

lines.line: Weak points: Winning a Bowser minigame only helps in part. In Bowser Balloon Burst everyone except the winner pays Bowser; in Face Lift only those who score under 90 do; in Tug o' War the side that loses does. Exceptions: a tie in Balloon Burst or Tug o' War costs every player 10 to 50 coins. If all four players reach 90 in Face Lift, Bowser takes up to 50 coins off the one who landed. In Bash 'n' Cash the one who landed wears the Bowser Suit: coins knocked out of them go to Bowser, and if they lose none he takes 15 from them.

quoted: Bowser Balloon Burst: The four players play the minigame Balloon Burst. Afterward, everyone aside from the winner of the minigame loses Coins to Bowser. If the minigame ends in a tie, everyone loses 10–50 Coins.

Bowser's Face Lift: The four players play the minigame Face Lift. Afterward, players that score fewer than 90 points lose Coins to Bowser. If all players achieve at least 90 points, Bowser steals up to 50 Coins from the player who landed on his space.

Bowser's Tug o' War: The four players play the minigame Tug o' War, with the player that landed on the Bowser Space taking on the role of the player in the Bowser Suit. Afterward, the losing side loses Coins to Bowser, but if the minigame ends in a tie, everybody loses 10–50 Coins.

Bash 'n' Cash: The four players play the minigame Bash 'n' Cash, with the player that landed on the Bowser Space taking on the role of the player in the Bowser Suit. Unlike normally, Coins knocked out of the player go straight to Bowser. If the player in the Bowser Suit does not lose any Coins during the minigame, Bowser takes 15 Coins from them.

lines.line: Tips: The Coins for Bowser event costs the player who landed 10 to 50 coins. Bowser Revolution gathers everyone's coins and shares them out in equal parts. In Bowser's Chance Time the coins always go to Bowser. The wheel also shows Star Steal, 100 Star Present and 1000 Coin Present in yellow text, but the pointer never stops on them. If you land on a Bowser Space with no coins but at least one Star, Bowser takes a Star and gives you 10 coins; if you have no coins and no Stars, he gives you 20 coins.

quoted: Coins for Bowser: Bowser takes 10–50 Coins from that player.
Bowser Revolution: Bowser takes everyone's Coins and splits them evenly among all the players.
it is rigged so that Bowser is always on the receiving end of the trade
100 Star Present / 1000 Coin Present / Star Steal: These events' names are displayed in yellow text on the roulette wheel. The cursor never lands on them.
If the player has at least one Star but no Coins, Bowser gives them 10 Coins in exchange for one Star.
If the player does not have any Coins or Stars, Bowser gives them 20 Coins.

lines.line: Summary: A ghost that haunts the boards and offers to steal for you: either some coins from a rival at no charge, or a Star at a cost of 50 coins. Every board has a Boo apart from Peach's Birthday Cake.

quoted: are recurring ghost enemies

Boos are on every board map except Peach's Birthday Cake, and they provide the player character with the option stealing either a number of coins from an opponent for free or a Star for 50 coins, on their behalf.

lines.line: Tips: On Luigi's Engine Room, whichever way you go, every path finishes at Warp Pipes leading to Boo, who stands close to the start. On Bowser's Magma Mountain, the free roulette at the purple Stone Head can send you to Boo. DK's Jungle Adventure is the only board with two Boos.

quoted: No matter where the players go, all paths end in Warp Pipes that lead to Boo, who is near the start.
Getting the Star picture takes them to Boo, and Bowser's face takes them to Bowser
Eventually, the player will reach a purple-colored Stone Head, who will offer the same roulette block, except free of charge.
It is also the only stage with two Boos.

lines.line: Summary: A guard on DK's Jungle Adventure that stands at a junction and lets you through only for 10 coins. The board has three.

quoted: Whomps guard some junctions in DK's Jungle Adventure in Mario Party. There are three Whomps, and paying them ten Coins is required to pass.

lines.line: Weak points: To pass a Whomp on the road it guards, you must pay 10 coins. You can instead take the road it is not watching, but then it shifts over to block the other road once you are through, leaving the first one open to the other three players.

quoted: paying them ten Coins is required to pass.
If a player chooses the route not guarded by a Whomp, it begins to block the route instead.
If a player does not pay Whomp, it blocks the other path after they move past it, which opens the initial path for the three other players.

lines.line: Looks like: Big rectangular stone slabs with jagged-toothed faces and, as with Thwomps, red eyes.

quoted: They are large enemies that resemble rectangular stone slabs with snaggletoothed faces
Like Thwomps, they have red eyes

lines.line: Tips: The Whomp keeps barring that same road for the other players, who must pay as well to get by. A Coin Stone lets a player through only if they hold 20 coins.

quoted: Whomp continues to block the same path against other players unless they also pay.
If a player encounters a Coin Stone, they can only pass it if they have 20 Coins.

lines.line: Summary: Two toll guards on the bridges between the two islands of Yoshi's Tropical Island. Each asks a fee to let you cross, starting at 1 coin and rising to a limit of 50.

quoted: Two Thwomps block the bridges to the opposite island, and request a fee from players if they want to pass to the other island.
The fee always starts at 1 Coin, but goes up by at least one Coin each time (at payers' discretion) until it reaches the limit of 50 Coins (in Mario Party
Up to fifty coins can be paid to the Thwomp before resetting.

lines.line: Looks like: The Thwomps here use a boxier take on the Super Mario 64 design.

quoted: Thwomps use a more cubic version of their Super Mario 64 design in the first six console games and Mario Party Advance.

lines.line: Tips: Landing on a Happening Space has Bubba the fish carry Toad over to the other island while Bowser steps into Toad's spot. Bowser charges 30 coins for a faulty Bowser Tube. Every lap around an island takes you past either Toad or Bowser. Each Thwomp has its own separate fee, and whoever crosses next has to hand over at least a coin more than the player before. A player who cannot afford the toll is stuck on the island they are on.

quoted: The Happening Spaces make Bubba the fish take Toad to the opposite island, Bowser taking his place. Bowser sells defective Bowser Tubes to players for 30 Coins.
a player must pass either Toad (Toadette in Superstars) or Bowser every time they circle an island
and the two Thwomps do not share the same fee.
must remain on the same island if they cannot afford to pay the toll to cross.
when another player tries to pass the Thwomp, they must pay at least one more coin than the previous player.

lines.line: Summary: A trap a rival can plant on Peach's Birthday Cake from a Happening Space for 30 coins. It steals a Star from an opponent who lands on its space and gives it to the player who planted it.

quoted: From a Happening Space, a player can pay 30 Coins to plant a Strawberry Seed
it will steal a Star from that player, and give it to the player that planted it.

lines.line: Weak points: It does nothing if you have no Stars when you land on it, it disappears once it has taken a Star, and it does nothing to the player who planted it.

quoted: though the Piranha Plant disappears after doing so and does nothing if the opponent has no Stars.
If a player lands on a space with their Piranha Plant or cannot afford to add one to an empty space, nothing occurs.

lines.line: Tips: Peach's Birthday Cake has 14 Happening Spaces, and the Strawberry Seed is planted from one of them.

quoted: Happening Spaces || 14
From a Happening Space, a player can pay 30 Coins to plant a Strawberry Seed

lines.line: Summary: A red board space that takes 3 coins from whoever lands on it, or 6 in the last five turns. Every board in the game has some.

quoted: If a player lands on this space, they lose 3 Coins. The amount of Coins lost is doubled during the Last Five Turns Event.
Red Spaces || 7
Red Spaces || 3

lines.line: Weak points: A Red Space costs the same 3 coins that a Blue Space pays, and both figures double during the final five turns, so each Blue Space stop cancels out one Red Space stop.

quoted: Players gain three Coins from landing on this. The amount of Coins received is doubled in the Last Five Turns Event.
If a player lands on this space, they lose 3 Coins. The amount of Coins lost is doubled during the Last Five Turns Event.

lines.line: Tips: On Bowser's Magma Mountain, landing on a Happening Space makes the volcano erupt and every Blue Space turns red, so the board has 49 Red Spaces instead of 4. The effect starts on the landing player's turn and runs out two turns later, again on that same player's turn. Red Spaces per board: DK's Jungle Adventure 7, Yoshi's Tropical Island 3, Peach's Birthday Cake 4, Wario's Battle Canyon 7, Luigi's Engine Room 4, Mario's Rainbow Castle 5, Bowser's Magma Mountain 4 and Eternal Star 3.

lines.line: Summary: A boulder that a Happening Space sets rolling on DK's Jungle Adventure. It sends any player in its way back toward the start.

quoted: If a player lands on one of the nine Happening Spaces spread throughout the board, a boulder begins to roll from the north-east, then left, then down Bowser's path.
Any players in the path of the rolling boulder try to escape it, but end up back towards the start

lines.line: Weak points: It only hits players caught in front of it as it rolls down Bowser's path, and a player it sweeps back still lands on a Blue Space and gets its three coins.

quoted: Any players in the path of the rolling boulder try to escape it, but end up back towards the start, landing on a Blue Space (which takes effect, granting them three Coins).
Landing on a Happening Space triggers a rolling boulder which, in turn, chases down any players standing in its way to the path near the start of the board.

lines.line: Tips: The board has nine Happening Spaces. When the game ends, the boulder chases whoever came fourth down the board.

quoted: If a player lands on one of the nine Happening Spaces spread throughout the board
At the end of the game, the winner joins all of their Stars together to form a giant one
The player in fourth place is chased down the board by a rolling boulder.

lines.line: Summary: A robot on Luigi's Engine Room that will switch the board's doors for 20 coins. Two of them are on the board.

quoted: Pisudon are robots from Mario Party. Two of them are found exclusively on the board Luigi's Engine Room.
for the price of 20 coins

lines.line: Tips: A Pisudon offers the switch when you cross paths with it, and the switch blocks certain paths for the other players.

quoted: the Pisudon offers them the option to switch the set of doors that rise up or go down throughout the board for the price of 20 coins, blocking access of certain paths to the other players.

lines.line: Summary: Useless things Bowser makes you buy when you walk by him on a board, a different one on each of six boards, for 10 to 40 coins.

quoted: Bowser's bogus items are useless items forcibly sold to partiers by Bowser in Mario Party when they pass him on a board.
Bowser sells this item to players for 10 coins.
However, the Ztar costs 40 coins as opposed to a regular Star costing 20, making it the most expensive of the bogus items.

lines.line: Uses: None of them helps you. The Gold-plated Bowser Statue is 10 coins on DK's Jungle Adventure, the Bowser Cake 20 on Peach's Birthday Cake, the Bowser Tube 30 on Yoshi's Tropical Island, Bowser's Claws or Cannon 20 on Wario's Battle Canyon, the Make As Many Coins As You Want Mecha 20 on Luigi's Engine Room, and the Ztar 40 on Mario's Rainbow Castle.

quoted: Bowser's bogus items are useless items forcibly sold to partiers by Bowser in Mario Party
Bowser sells this item to players for 10 coins. It looks like a miniature version of the Koopa King, and is completely worthless.
he forcibly gives the player this item for 20 coins.
Bowser demands 30 coins for buying (and in this case, popping) his merchandise
The player will pay 20 coins (or all their coins if they have 20 or less) for the ride
Bowser activates this machine in order to create a coin for the player at the cost of 20 coins
Bowser forces the player to buy a Ztar.

lines.line: Looks like: The Gold-plated Bowser Statue is a small model of the Koopa King, the Bowser Cake is a spiked shell topped by a candle and some frosting, and the Ztar is a black star with white eyes.

quoted: It looks like a miniature version of the Koopa King, and is completely worthless.
It is just a spiked shell with a candle and frosting, and cannot be eaten.
They appear as black stars with white eyes.

lines.line: Tips: Bowser's Claws shoot you off to a random place on the board. The price is 20 coins, or all of yours if you hold 20 or fewer, and nothing if you hold none. The Make As Many Coins As You Want Mecha hands back one coin for the 20 you pay, so you are down 19. Straight after you "buy" the Ztar you walk by Koopa Troopa and get 10 coins back. That rises to 20 in the final five turns or when it is the tenth time anyone has gone by him, to 30 on the twentieth time, and onward. On Bowser's Magma Mountain and Eternal Star he sells nothing; he takes a Star instead, or else up to 20 coins from a player who has no Star.

quoted: The player will pay 20 coins (or all their coins if they have 20 or less) for the ride, though Bowser will give it to them for free if they have zero coins.
blast the player to a random area of the board
thus meaning the player loses 19 coins, due to the one coin they get from the machine.

immediately after "buying" the Ztar, the player will pass Koopa Troopa and earn back 10 coins (20 in the last 5 turns or if it is the 10th time someone has passed Koopa Troopa; 30 for the 20th time; 40 for the 30th time; etc.)

Bowser does not sell any useless items or provide a worthless service on either Bowser's Magma Mountain or Eternal Star, where he steals either a Star or up to 20 coins if they do not have at least one Star.

lines.line: Summary: A 200-coin Mushroom Shop item that hides a visit from Bowser, Koopa Troopa or Boo on one space of the board.

quoted: It is bought at the Mushroom Shop for 200 Coins
It is hidden in one of the spaces on the board, and when a player lands on that space, the Event Block appears. The player would then get one of three events: Boo, Koopa Troopa, or Bowser.

lines.line: Uses: When a player lands on the hidden space, Koopa Troopa drops in and hands them 20 coins; Boo does his usual theft of coins or a Star; or Bowser takes 20 coins, or whatever they have if it is less, and gives a single coin to a player with none.

quoted: Boo steals Coins or a Star like normal. Koopa Troopa falls from the sky, gives the player 20 Coins then walks off screen.
He takes away 20 Coins or however many the player has if they have fewer. If they have none, Bowser gives them one coin

lines.line: Tips: Once bought, you can switch it on or off at the bank. Bowser's coin is wiped out when the player is on a Red Space.

quoted: upon buying it, it can be turned on and off at the bank.
The coin given by Bowser is canceled out if they are on a Red Space.

sections.name: Coin Box, Lucky Box and Casino Box

lines.line: Summary: Three boxes that keep your coins and Stars safe once a board game is over: the Coin Box you are given first, the 400-coin Lucky Box and the 300-coin Casino Box.

quoted: This is the first item given when the game begins. Its purpose is to store coins and Stars that players acquire at the end of a board game (or Mini-Game Stadium).
It can be purchased from the Mushroom Shop in Mushroom Village for 400 coins.
Like the Coin Box, the Lucky Box stores coins and Stars
It can be bought in the Mushroom Shop for 300 coins.
It stores coins and Stars like the Coin Box

lines.line: Uses: The Lucky Box gives you an extra 10% of each round's coin total. After every game the Casino Box spins a roulette: x2 doubles the coins you put in, -1/2 throws out half of them, and 0 changes nothing.

quoted: after every round of partying, the player earns an additional 10% coin bonus from that round's total.
after every game, it gives the player a chance to win more or lose some coins by roulette.
the coin amount deposited is doubled.
half the deposited coins are spat out.
does nothing.

lines.line: Tips: The Casino Box has a cap of 100 Stars and 99,999 coins. At the Mushroom Bank, Porto is where you pick which to save with: the Casino Box, Lucky Box or Coin Box. Storing at the game's end happens for human-controlled players only.

quoted: The Casino Box can hold a maximum of 99,999 coins and 100 Stars.
Here is also where the player can choose how they want to save their Coins, whether with the Coin Box, Lucky Box, or Casino Box.
However, only human-controlled players will have their coins and Stars stored at the end of the board game.

lines.line: Summary: Two 500-coin Mushroom Shop items, one named for Koopa Troopa and one for Boo.

quoted: No Koopa || 500 Coins
No Boo || 500 Coins

lines.line: Uses: While No Koopa is active, Koopa Troopa does not hand you the 10 coins for passing the starting point.

quoted: Koopa Troopa awards a player 10 coins each time they pass the starting point in Mario Party, unless the No Koopa item is active or the player is playing on Eternal Star.

lines.line: Tips: You must finish the Eternal Star map before either item can be bought.

quoted: The Eternal Star map must be completed before obtaining the item.

lines.line: Summary: A board space that spins a roulette between a Mushroom, which gives you another roll, and a Poisonous Mushroom, which costs you your next turn.

quoted: A roulette block appears if a player lands on this space. Either the player can receive a Mushroom, which gives the Player the chance to roll another Dice Block, or receive a Poison Mushroom, which forces them to forfeit their next turn's Dice Block roll.

lines.line: Uses: The Mushroom lets you roll again. The Poisonous Mushroom costs you your next turn.

quoted: It triggers a roulette block with a Mushroom, which allows the player to roll again, and a Poisonous Mushroom, which costs them their next turn.

lines.line: Summary: A rare board space marked with an exclamation mark that starts Chance Time, where three Dice Blocks decide who gives what to whom.

quoted: Chance Time Spaces (known as ! Spaces in the first three Mario Party games) are among the rarest type of spaces in the Mario Party series.

The first Mario Party establishes Chance Time as rolling three Dice Blocks, lined up from left to right. The left and right blocks correspond to the four player characters in the game, while the middle one specifies how many coins or Stars one must give to the other.

lines.line: Uses: The middle block can make one player give 10, 20 or 30 coins or 1 Star to the other, and two more results, marked with a double arrow, swap all coins or all Stars.

quoted: 10 coins → - ← 10 coins - 20 coins → - ← 20 coins - 30 coins → - ← 30 coins - 1 Star → - ← 1 Star - ↔ all coins - ↔ all Stars
icon for "swap all coins and stars"
Game-changing events can happen here, from trading Stars or Coins, to giving one Star or 10-30 Coins to someone else.

lines.line: Tips: You can roll the three blocks in whatever order you like. Once you choose a character on one side, that character is gone from the other side, and each roll makes the blocks go faster. In the first game a ! Space counts as a Blue Space, and where the Star relocates after someone buys it, the ! Space is put on the spot the Star last stood on. Bowser's Chance Time, one of the Bowser Space events, is rigged: from the start the blocks whirl too fast to control, Bowser is locked in on the right block, and a loser with nothing gets 10 coins from Bowser, out of pity.

quoted: The player landing on the "! Space" can roll the dice in any order. Selecting a character on either side block removes the character from the other side, so they cannot appear on both at once. The blocks speed up after each roll.

Here, the blocks spin uncontrollably fast from the outset, the middle block's options are to only give coins from left to right, and the right block is preset to Bowser. If the loser has no coins, Bowser will give them 10 coins out of pity.
In the first game, on boards where the Star moves after a player purchases one, a ! Space will take the space where the Star has been. In the first game as well, they count as Blue Spaces.

sections.name: Gameballs, Mecha Fly Guy, Talking Parrot and Record

lines.line: Summary: Four of the Mushroom Shop's items, priced 50 to 300 coins: Gameballs, the Mecha Fly Guy, the Talking Parrot and the Record.

quoted: Gameballs || 300 Coins
Mecha Fly Guy || 100 Coins
Record || 50 Coins
Talking Parrot || 50 Coins

lines.line: Uses: Gameballs cost 300 coins and the Mecha Fly Guy costs 100. There is a Mecha Fly Guy in the Mini-Game House.

quoted: Gameballs || 300 Coins
Mecha Fly Guy || 100 Coins
In the Mini-Game House, there is a Mecha Fly Guy that is sold in the Mushroom Shop for 100 coins.

lines.line: Tips: Gameballs turn up in the shop once you have bought 30 or more mini-games at the Mini-Game House, and stay usable until every mini-game there is bought. The Record, at 50 coins, is what unlocks the Option House's Juke Box, and only for songs you have already heard in the game. The 50-coin Talking Parrot plays random character voices there when you press its button.

quoted: This item appears after at least 30 mini-games have been bought from the Mini-Game House and can be used until all mini-games are bought.
The Juke Box becomes available for use after the player buys the Record from the Mushroom Shop for 50 Coins.
The only prerequisite is that the player must have heard the song in the game itself before it becomes available on the Juke Box.
By pressing the button, the parrot speaks various voices from various characters in the game randomly.
